 The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan is launching its annual holiday campaign today to help feed thousands of families in need.
 FLINT, Mich. (WJRT) - The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan launched its annual holiday campaign to help feed thousands of families in need.
 The "Harvesting Hope, Nourishing Neighbors" campaign kicked off with a mobile food distribution at Every Nation Assembly of God in Flint, with the goal of raising money and distributing food across 22 counties.
 "We have all of these great volunteers working here and food distributions going on, and we feel really good about distributing 38 million pounds of food a year, but sadly it's not enough," said Kara Ross, president and CEO of the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan. "We have over 234,000 people in our service area experiencing food insecurity, and many of them for the very first time. So all of the challenges you can think of the cost of groceries, rising fuel costs, we're getting into the heating season, you know, Michigan winter and everybody that needs the help can go to this network. It's a charitable network of food providers for just that type of emergency."
 Over the past 45 years, the food bank has grown to distribute more than 37 million pounds of food annually through nearly 700 partner agencies.
 Anyone who would like to support to campaign or receive assistance, checkout fbem.org.
